fatal_errors: The proposed Al alloying and precipitation treatment does not reconstruct the target intervention, which is laser-assisted machining of DED-fabricated Ti33Nb28Cr11V11Ni17.

No explicit alloy composition is supplied, so compliance with the five-element, 5–35 at% definition and preservation of Ti and Ni as primary constituents cannot be verified; the proposed 3 at% Al endpoint is itself below the stated minimum.
The cited evidence establishes gamma/gamma-prime behavior in a Ni-Co-Fe-Cr-Al-Ti alloy, not coherent gamma-prime formation from 3–5 at% Al in an unspecified Ti-Ni-primary alloy.
explanation: This is a testable but speculative alternative rather than a reconstruction. It addresses the literal goal of improving elevated-temperature strength and gives a matched no-Al baseline, microstructural measurements, mechanical tests, and a quantitative falsification threshold. However, it misses every central feature of the hidden study: DED Ti33Nb28Cr11V11Ni17, laser preheating near the machining tool, thermal softening above about 800 °C, and reductions in cutting force, roughness, and work hardening relative to conventional machining. Its gamma-prime mechanism is only indirectly supported because phase stability depends strongly on the full composition, which is not specified. The 3–5 at% intervention range also partly violates the stated HEA constituent range.
